cohort: The study included 744 mothers from randomly selected households in a rural area of Tanzania who had children aged less than five years.
finding: Higher levels of social capital were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of delivering in a health facility.
mod_finding: Increased social capital was found to significantly increase the odds of delivering in a health facility, which implies a preference for skilled birth attendance.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from mothers of children aged less than five years regarding the place of delivery of their last child.
